text:
The Nifty 50 edged higher to 25,299.35, up 0.18% on the day, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 0.36% to 23,865.8. Gains were modest but broad‑based, with 294 advances versus 191 declines in the Nifty 500 universe, giving a breadth score of 75.1 (a “healthy” market). The India VIX, a volatility gauge, fell 5.35% to 16.62, indicating reduced fear. Bank Nifty outperformed, up 1.19% to 61,518.5, reflecting strength in the banking sector.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers, adding ₹7,830.6 crore, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold ₹6,331.2 crore, extending an 11‑day buying streak for FIIs and a 9‑day selling streak for DIIs. Leading sectors were PSU banks, capital markets, financial services, realty, private banks, auto and consumption, while media, pharma, IT and infrastructure showed weakening signs. Options data show a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 0.85 for Nifty (bullish bias) and 1.28 for Bank Nifty (slightly bearish). The “max pain” levels – where most options expire worthless – sit at 25,200 for Nifty and 59,000 for Bank Nifty, with expected trading ranges of 24,987‑25,612 and 60,235‑62,802 respectively.

Watch the 25,275.7 pivot (P) and the first support at 25,166.6 for Nifty; a break below 24,000 (put wall) could test deeper lows. For Bank Nifty, the pivot is 61,262.5 with support at 60,979.1; a move past the 58,000 put wall may signal further weakness. Key headlines to monitor include RBI rate‑hike concerns, global oil price moves (Brent at $95.65) and any fresh volatility from the tech sector, as these could influence the next session’s direction.
